title: Last moment a permit can be consumed

request.goal: authority = PermitAuthority(default_ttl_seconds=900, clock=clock). While clock() returns 1000.0, a permit is issued with issue(capability, scope, basis, ttl_seconds=600). Later consume() is called with the matching capability and scope. What is the largest clock() value at which that consume() still succeeds?

code.title: scripts/capability_permits.py excerpt (ttl and expiry)
code.text:
def __init__(self, ledger_path: Path | None = None, *, default_ttl_seconds: float = 900,
                 clock=time.time, max_cumulative_usd: float | None = None):
        ...
        self.default_ttl = default_ttl_seconds
        self.clock = clock
    ...
        ttl = self.default_ttl if ttl_seconds is None else ttl_seconds
        require(0 < ttl <= 86_400, "invalid_permit_ttl")
        ...
        now = self.clock()
        ...
            "issued_at": now, "expires_at": now + ttl,
    ...
    def consume(self, permit_id: str, capability: str, scope: dict) -> dict:
        ...
            require(grant["scope_hash"] == digest(scope), "permit_scope_mismatch")
            require(self.clock() <= grant["expires_at"], "permit_expired")

pass: 1600.0: the explicit ttl_seconds=600 overrides the 900 default, so expires_at = 1000 + 600 = 1600, and consume() requires clock() <= expires_at, so exactly 1600.0 still succeeds.
The largest value is 1600 (the check is <=, so 1600 itself is allowed).
**expires_at = 1600.0**; consume works up to and including that instant.
fail: Just below 1600, because consume uses < expires_at.
The largest value is 1900; ttl_seconds only applies to new authorities.
